findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing `?` and bypasses `untrusted_attributes` restrictions
findings.body:
`ActiveModel::Serializer` expects conditional inclusion methods to end with a question mark (`include_website_name?`). Because `def include_website_name` has no trailing `?`, it is never called and `website_name` is always serialized into the JSON output (even as `nil` when the user has no website).

In addition, `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) so that TL0 users' profile URLs are hidden from anonymous visitors via `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`, but `website_name` is not. As a result, a TL0 user's website host/path is still exposed in the JSON and rendered as text on the user profile page for anonymous users. Adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (and removing `def include_website_name`) will define `include_website_name?` with both the trust-level restriction and `.present?` check.

findings.title: Domain comparison mishandles multi-part TLDs and subdomains of apex instance domains
findings.body:
The domain matching logic in `website_name` has two flaws:

1. In the `elsif` branch, comparing `split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` whenever both hosts have the same number of labels (`> 2`) treats any two unrelated domains under a two-level public suffix (e.g. `discourse_host = 'example.co.uk'` and `website_host = 'other.co.uk'`, or `.com.au`, `.org.uk`) as the same domain because both strip the first label and match on `'co.uk'`.
2. When the Discourse instance is hosted on an apex domain (e.g. `example.com`) and the user's website is on a subdomain such as `http://www.example.com/user` or `http://blog.example.com/user`, `website_host == discourse_host` is false, the `elsif` branch is skipped because label counts differ (`3 != 2`), and the `else` branch checks `'example.com'.ends_with?('.www.example.com')` which is false, so the path is unexpectedly omitted.

findings.title: `website_name` is not updated on the user model after saving preferences
findings.body: Previously, `websiteName` was a client-side computed property on the controller observing `model.website`, so saving a new `website` in user preferences updated the displayed website name immediately. Now that `website_name` is computed on the server, `User#save` (around line 210, where `self.set('bio_excerpt', data.user.bio_excerpt)` is updated from the `PUT /users/:username` response) does not copy `data.user.website_name` onto the model, leaving `model.website_name` stale or blank when navigating back to the user profile without a full page reload.
